figures.caption: Figure 1: Eigenvalues λn of the evolution operator for different values of refractory period τ0. Current mean µ is varied at 0.1mV steps keeping D = 8mV2. (a) Real part of λn; (b) imaginary part. Red and blue branches are mixed and real λn, respectively. Different shadings represent τ0 from 0 τm (light) to 0.4 τm (dark). Parameters: τm = 1, H = 0 mV, θ = 20 mV, α = −5θ = −100 mV,

Figure 2: Defective eigenvalues at the real-to-complex transition in a mixed branch. (a) Real part of ∆γ(s) for three mean currents around the transition, µ = 9.94, 10.06 (exceptional point) and 10.18 mV; intersections with the horizontal axis are real λn. (b) The same transition (second mixed branch in Figure 1) in the complex plane of the eigenvalues; light to dark points, increasing µ from 9.94 to 10.18 mV. (c) Inverse leading coefficient 1/|Zn| across the transition, evaluated from the biorthogonal scalar product 1/⟨ψn, ϕn⟩ (grey) and from the closed form 1/∆′ γ(λn) (red); the two agree away from the transition and both diverge at the exceptional point (dashed line), where ∆γ acquires a second-order zero. (d) Modulus of the self-coupling coefficient Cµ nn = ⟨∂µψn, ϕn⟩, which diverges at the same point: the modal decomposition ceases to be well defined at a defective eigenvalue. Parameters: D = 8mV2, H = 0 mV, θ = 20 mV, τ0 = 0, τm = 1.

Figure 3: Module (left) and phase (right) of the transfer function in response to a noise (HD, top) and drift (Hµ, bottom) sinusoidal perturbation with (dotted line, τ0 = 0.1τm) or without (solid lines, τ0 = 0) absolute refractory period. Vertical dashed lines, Imλn ≃ 2πnν0; the abscissa is the ordinary frequency ω/2π in units of τ−1

Figure 4: (a) Locus of the leading eigenvalues (poles) of the coupled system as the refractory period τ0 is varied; the inset magnifies the pair closest to the imaginary axis. The crossing of the imaginary axis by the diffusion poles indicates a Hopf bifurcation and the onset of global oscillations. (b) Population firing rate ν(t) from the corresponding Fokker–Planck simulations at τ0 = 0, 0.05 and 0.1 τm (top to bottom): the damped relaxation towards ν0 (dashed) at τ0 = 0 gives way to a sustained limit cycle once the diffusion pair has crossed. Same parameters as Figure 3, with K = 1000, J = 0.012 (KJ = 12) and transmission delay τD = 0.2 τm
